settings.subAgent.exploreHint: Read-only investigation — it cannot change anything. A cheap model does fine.
settings.subAgent.agentHint: Inherits the main assistant's tools, so it can edit files and run commands.
settings.general.title: General
settings.general.shellHint: Shell used by the run_command tool. Bash (Git Bash) is recommended for UTF-8 support.
settings.general.sandboxContainerHint: Commands run in a Docker container belonging to this conversation, so what they install stays for the next command and what they touch stays inside the project. Needs Docker running, and needs the conversation to belong to a project. Custom command tools go in too, so any that depend on this machine's toolchain will stop working.
settings.general.sandboxHint: Windows only. run_command runs under a restricted-token sandbox limited to writing the project directory and TEMP; blocked commands ask whether to retry without sandbox. Network access is not restricted. Note: Git Bash cannot start inside the sandbox (every command will ask for escalation) — switch the shell to PowerShell or CMD when the sandbox is on.
settings.general.searchHint: API key for the web_search tool. The model will use this to search the web for current information.

settings.fileAccess.description: Grant the assistant access to files on this device. The system won't prompt again after granting, but every file operation still requires your approval in the chat.
settings.fileAccess.manageHint: Allow access to the entire shared storage (/storage/emulated/0). Requires a system-level grant.
settings.fileAccess.manageNotGranted: Not granted by the system yet. Allow "All files access" on the settings page that opened, then return to the app.
settings.fileAccess.approvalNote: The assistant asks for your approval in the chat before reading, writing, moving, or deleting any file. You can deny with a reason.

settings.model.pricePairError: Input and output prices must either both be set or both be blank
settings.model.tierNeedsBaseError: Price tiers need the base input and output prices filled in first
settings.model.priceInvalidError: “{{field}}” is not a valid price; enter a decimal number such as 0.5
settings.model.cachePriceHint: Blank bills at the input rate
settings.model.cacheWritePriceHint: Blank bills at the input rate; Anthropic charges 1.25–2x
settings.model.priceTiersHint: Rates that replace the ones above once a prompt reaches the threshold. The whole request is repriced, not just the excess, and the threshold counts cached tokens too. Grok 4.6 doubles every rate above 200000.
settings.model.serverToolsHint: Run by the provider instead of by this app: no API key of ours, no approval prompt, and the results never pass through the context window. Switching web search on removes the built-in one from this model's tools. Billed separately from tokens.
settings.model.serverToolPriceHint: Charged on top of the tokens. xAI bills $5 per 1000 for web search, X search and code execution alike. Blank means unpriced — the calls still happen and are counted, they just add nothing to the total.
settings.model.capabilitiesHint: Only needed when the built-in catalog is wrong or missing this model. "Auto" keeps following catalog updates.
chat.context.title: Context usage
toolbar.acceptEdits.hint: Edit files inside the project without asking each time. Still asks about anything outside the project, about deletes and moves, and about files like .git that make code run later.
settings.acp.title: Claude Code sessions
settings.acp.subtitle: Run Claude Code inside Meridian, over the Agent Client Protocol.
settings.acp.commandHint: The ACP adapter is a node package and is not bundled. The default runs it straight from npm.
settings.acp.argsHint: One per line, so an argument containing a space stays one argument.
settings.acp.saveBeforeCheck: Save first — the test runs the saved command
settings.acp.authNote: Sessions sign in as whatever `claude` is signed in as on this machine. If a session fails to start, run `claude` in a terminal once and log in there.
settings.autoReview.title: Automatic approval review
settings.autoReview.description: Let a second model answer the approvals you would otherwise be asked for, and say why it decided as it did.
settings.autoReview.enableHint: Only the calls that would have interrupted you are reviewed — reads inside the project and, in accept-edits mode, writes inside it, never reach a reviewer at all. If it cannot reach a verdict you are asked as before; in a QQ chat, where nobody is there to ask, it refuses.
settings.autoReview.modelHint: Reviews happen while you wait for the tool call, so a fast model is worth more here than a clever one. Its tokens are billed to you and counted separately under Usage.
settings.autoReview.noModel: Nothing will be reviewed until a model is chosen.
settings.autoReview.escalate: Look at the repository when unsure
settings.autoReview.escalateHint: A verdict of deny, a dangerous allow, or an unreadable answer earns a second pass with four read-only tools — enough to find out what `rm -rf $TARGET` actually points at. Slower, and the reason most refusals turn out to be correct.
settings.approvals.ttlHint: Minutes a permission card may stand before the question is withdrawn. Withdrawing is not refusing: the tool does not run, and the turn carries on and says so. 0 keeps a card up indefinitely.
settings.approvals.ttlNever: Cards will stand until answered. A turn nobody comes back to holds its conversation open.
settings.autoReview.environmentHint: What the reviewer should take as given: which hosts are yours, what this machine is for, which directories are scratch space.
settings.autoReview.environmentPlacehold:
One per line, e.g.
git.example.com is our own server
~/tmp is scratch space and may be deleted freely
settings.autoReview.allowHint: Things you do not want to be asked about again. These widen what gets approved, so keep them specific.
settings.autoReview.allowPlaceholder:
One per line, e.g.
Running the test suite, including outside the project
settings.autoReview.denyHint: Things that must never be approved on your behalf, whatever the reviewer thinks.
settings.autoReview.denyPlaceholder:
One per line, e.g.
Anything that pushes to a remote
Anything touching ~/.ssh
settings.voiceCorpus.title: Stored Voice
settings.voiceCorpus.description: Voice notes kept from the sessions on the OneBot allowlist, with their transcripts. Sessions are shown under a pseudonym.
settings.voiceCorpus.empty: Nothing stored. Voice is only kept for sessions you list under OneBot.
settings.voiceCorpus.deleteSessionConfir: Delete every recording in “{{handle}}”? This cannot be undone.
settings.voiceCorpus.deletedWithFailures: Deleted {{clips}} clips; {{failures}} files could not be removed and will be retried.
settings.voiceCorpus.forgetSenderHint: Deletes everything they sent, across sessions, and stops recording them from now on. Two separate things, done together because that is what the request usually means.
settings.voiceCorpus.forgetSenderConfirm: Forget “{{sender}}”? Their recordings will be deleted permanently and future recordings from them will be blocked.
settings.voiceCorpus.forgot: Deleted {{clips}} clips and stopped recording them.
settings.voiceCorpus.exportHint: Writes manifest.jsonl plus an audio/ directory. Sessions and speakers are pseudonymous by default — stable within this installation, not linkable outside it, and not reversible to a QQ number.
settings.voiceCorpus.includeSender: Write real QQ numbers instead of pseudonyms
settings.voice.title: Voice Input
settings.voice.intro: Fully offline speech-to-text. The model runs locally; recordings never leave your device.
settings.voice.modelHint: About 127 MB, downloaded once; app updates never re-download it.
settings.voice.deleteModelConfirm: Delete the downloaded recognition model? It must be downloaded or imported again before voice input works.
settings.voice.mirrorPlaceholder: Leave empty for the default source (GitHub)
settings.voice.mirrorHint: If GitHub is slow, point this at a mirror of the same .tar.bz2 archive.
settings.voice.filterHint: Cleans up "um, uh, like" fillers before sending. Standard removes interjections and stutters; aggressive also drops trailing filler phrases.
settings.onebot.title: OneBot Service
settings.onebot.enableHint: Accept reverse WebSocket connections from OneBot clients (Lagrange, NapCat, etc.)
settings.onebot.assistantHint: Which assistant to use for bot conversations
settings.onebot.adminUsersHint: Comma-separated. Admins can approve tool calls via chat.
settings.onebot.voiceSend: Let the assistant reply with its voice
settings.onebot.voiceSendHint: Off by default. The text to be spoken is sent to Fish Audio; the free tier may be used to improve their models and is announced as free only until 2026-08-31. Paid models cost money per request.
settings.onebot.voiceNotReady: Voice replies are not in effect yet — {{missing}} is still empty. Until all four are set the assistant cannot see the tool, so asking it only gets you "I have no voice tool".
settings.onebot.voiceSendGroupsHint: Private chats are allowed by default — one counterpart, and they are the one listening. A group is a room, so whether voice is welcome there is the room's decision. Written <bot>@group:123, comma-separated.
settings.onebot.voiceTtsModelHint: No default — pick one and verify it works. s2.1-pro-free is free until 2026-08-31; the others bill per request.
settings.onebot.voiceTtsVoiceHint: A fixed voice from your Fish Audio library. The bot's voice is an identity, not a per-message choice.
settings.onebot.fishKeyHint: Stored in the OS keychain. Voice replies need all four: this key, a model, a voice id, and the switch above.
settings.onebot.voiceCaptureHint: Off everywhere unless listed. Written <bot>@group:123 or <bot>@private:456, comma-separated. These are recordings of real people — tell the group. Removing an entry takes effect at once, but does not delete what was already kept.
settings.onebot.ackEmojiHint: QQ emoji ID used to react to group messages (76 = thumbs up). Empty or 0 disables.
settings.onebot.invalidAdmins: Admin user IDs must be positive whole numbers separated by commas or spaces.
settings.onebot.invalidVoiceCapture: Voice capture entries must use bot@group:id or bot@private:id.
settings.onebot.invalidVoiceSend: Voice send entries must use bot@group:id.
settings.onebot.loadError: OneBot settings could not be loaded.
settings.hooks.title: Plan review gate
settings.hooks.enableHint: Whether Meridian starts this service on launch. Leaving it off still lets you start the service by hand below; it just will not come back next time. What the service does: lets a coding agent such as Claude Code send its plan here for review before it leaves plan mode.
settings.hooks.reviewModelHint: Required. The reviewer gets four read-only tools: it can read the repository under review and change nothing in it.
settings.hooks.assistantHint: Only temperature, thinking and the rest come from it; the persona is always the review prompt.
settings.hooks.timeoutHint: Past this the plan is not blocked and goes to you as usual. Capped at 1200s: the plugin gives up at 1260 and Claude Code kills the hook at 1320, and the three have to decrease or nobody gets to say it timed out. Reviewing a real plan takes minutes — it checks the plan's claims against the repository one by one — so do not set this short.
settings.hooks.maxRoundsHint: After this many rejections in a row the gate stops blocking and the plan goes to you as usual, findings included. Set 0 to remove this limit.
settings.hooks.maxRoundsUnlimited: No limit. Still safe: a plan that goes two rounds without material change is treated as not converging and let through — that check measures progress rather than counting rounds.
settings.hooks.tokenHint: The plugin reads this from the handshake file; there is nothing to copy. Checked even on loopback: every process on this machine, and every page in your browser, can reach that port.
settings.hooks.regenerateConfirm: Generate a new hook token? Existing integrations will stop working until they are updated.
settings.hooks.invalidNumbers: Enter a port from 1–65535, a timeout from 10–1200 seconds, and rounds from 0–20.
settings.hooks.loadError: Hook settings could not be loaded.
settings.remote.title: Remote access
settings.remote.subtitle: Let another device — a phone, a tablet, the laptop in the next room — use this desktop. Nothing is copied or synchronised: the other device is looking at the same conversations this window is, and a turn it starts runs here.
settings.remote.enable: Serve this desktop to other devices
settings.remote.enableHint: Whether Meridian starts this server on launch. Leaving it off still lets you start the server by hand below; it just will not come back next time.
settings.remote.trustWarning: Any device holding the token can read and write every conversation and run everything this app can run. The token is the whole credential — there is no second factor and no per-device approval. Give it only to devices that are yours.
settings.remote.hostHint: 0.0.0.0 is every interface, which is the point. On 127.0.0.1 nothing but this machine can reach it.
settings.remote.tokenHint: Generated here, and typed into the other device once. Not editable on purpose: the server refuses a public address with a token shorter than 16 characters, and a token you can type is a token you can make guessable.
settings.remote.tokenPending: Generated the first time you turn this on
settings.remote.regenerateConfirm: A new token disconnects every device currently connected, and each of them has to be given the new one before it can come back. Continue?
settings.remote.loadError: Remote access settings could not be loaded.
settings.remote.addressesHint: Type one of these into the other device, which has to be on the same network as this machine. If none of them answer, the firewall on this machine is the usual reason.
settings.remote.addressesEmpty: No address found — this machine may not be on a network.
settings.client.title: This device's connection
settings.client.intro: Leave this empty to use the Meridian on this machine. Fill it in to use another one instead — turn on Remote access over there first, and copy the address and token it shows you.
settings.client.tokenHint: The one the other machine generated. It is kept in this device's keychain, never in the page.
settings.client.testUnreachable: Nothing answered at that address. Check that the other machine is on the same network, that Remote access is running over there, and that its firewall allows the port.
settings.client.testMalformed: Something answered, but it was not Meridian.
settings.client.testClientOld: This is a version problem, not an address problem: that machine speaks revision {{apiRev}} and needs a client of at least {{minClientRev}}, and this app is older than that. Update this device.
settings.client.testServerOld: This is a version problem, not an address problem: that machine speaks revision {{apiRev}} and this app expects a newer one. Update Meridian over there.
settings.client.disconnectHint: Everything else on this page belongs to the machine you are connected to. Disconnecting reloads the app and brings back this device's own Meridian; nothing is deleted either side.
settings.client.composerOffline: Not connected — reconnecting. Nothing can be sent until the other machine answers.
capability.exportToDisk: Not available while connected to another machine: the file would be written to that machine's disk, not this one.
capability.importFromDisk: Not available while connected to another machine: the file has to be readable by the machine running Meridian, and this device's picker cannot see its disk.

settings.skills.subtitle: Skills are folders of instructions the model can open on demand. Bind one to load it into every conversation.
settings.skills.dirNameHint: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. This is also the name the model sees, so it cannot be changed later.
settings.skills.dirNameInvalid: Use lowercase letters, digits and hyphens only, starting and ending with a letter or digit.
settings.skills.descriptionHint: One line telling the model when this skill is worth opening.
settings.skills.bodyHint: Markdown instructions the model reads after it opens the skill.
settings.skills.globalBindingHint: Globally bound skills are announced in every conversation, which costs context on every message.

planReview.source.reason.raw_html: This plan contains raw HTML, so it is shown as Markdown source to preserve it exactly.
planReview.source.reason.image: This plan contains images, so it is shown as Markdown source to preserve them exactly.
planReview.source.reason.footnote: This plan contains footnotes, so it is shown as Markdown source to preserve them exactly.
planReview.source.reason.heading_level: This plan uses deeper headings than the rich editor supports, so it is shown as source.
planReview.source.reason.table: This plan contains a table, so it is shown as Markdown source to preserve it exactly.
planReview.source.reason.task_list: This plan contains a task list, so it is shown as Markdown source to preserve it exactly.
planReview.source.reason.editor_schema: This draft was saved by another editor schema, so it is shown as source instead of being converted silently.
planReview.source.reason.saved_source: This draft was saved in source mode, so it stays in source mode to preserve its text and comment ranges.
planReview.source.reason.unsupported: This plan uses Markdown the rich editor cannot preserve exactly, so it is shown as source.
planReview.source.reason.malformed: This plan could not be converted losslessly, so it is shown as Markdown source.

settings.ime.title: Meridian input method
settings.ime.subtitle: A Windows input method that installs with Meridian: pinyin and zhuyin, with candidates and learning entirely on this machine. It does not need Meridian to run — close this window and keep typing; this page is only where it is set up.
settings.ime.notInstalled: This build does not ship the input method
settings.ime.hostStopped: Registered; the service is not running
settings.ime.protocolMismatch: protocol differs from this build; restart the service
settings.ime.registerHint: Registration asks for administrator approval once: the DLL is added to the system-wide list of text services, which is the only place Windows reads it from. The installer normally does this; the button is for repairs.
settings.ime.enableForUserHint: Adds “Meridian 输入法” to this account’s input switcher (Win+Space). No administrator needed, and other accounts are untouched.
settings.ime.schemeHint: The scheme used under the zh-CN profile; the zh-TW profile is always zhuyin. Changes apply within a second, no restart.
settings.ime.learningHint: Remembers the words you pick and what follows what, and builds new words from them. The data is a few readable text files under ime/learn on this machine, and nothing is ever learned in password fields or in the programs listed below.
settings.ime.privateAppsHint: One executable name per line. The input method works normally in these; it just remembers nothing.
settings.ime.debugLog: Log every key to the service log
settings.ime.dictionariesEmpty: No dictionary yet; import one to type. rime-ice’s rime_ice.dict.yaml is the recommended start.
settings.ime.dictionariesHint: Dictionaries do not ship with the installer: import a Rime .dict.yaml and it is converted, together with the tables it imports, into the local format. The licence stays the dictionary’s own.
settings.ime.importing: Converting; a large dictionary takes seconds to a minute.
settings.ime.importCached: {{name}} was already up to date; nothing rebuilt
settings.ime.removeConfirm: Remove the dictionary “{{name}}”? The converted file is deleted; the original .dict.yaml is untouched.
settings.ime.limitations: Known limits: the candidate window can be hidden behind system surfaces such as Start menu search; there is no language-bar button yet; traditional output needs a traditional dictionary.
settings.ime.loadError: Could not load the input method settings.
